arxiv-2104-14197.title: Hybrid model with viscous relativistic hydrodynamics: a role of constraints on the shear-stress tensor
arxiv-2104-14197.creator: A. S. Khvorostukhin, E. E. Kolomeitsev, V. D. Toneev
arxiv-2104-14197.description: Abstract We present the hybrid hadron string dynamic (HydHSD) model connecting the parton-hadron-string dynamic model (PHSD) and a hydrodynamic model taking into account shear viscosity within the Israel-Stewart approach. The numerical scheme, initialization, and particlization procedure are discussed in detail.

arxiv-2303-10541.title: Animating Explosions
arxiv-2303-10541.creator: Gary D. Yngve, James F. O’Brien, Jessica K. Hodgins
arxiv-2303-10541.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce techniques for animating explosions and their effects. The primary effect of an explosion is a disturbance that causes a shock wave to propagate through the surrounding medium. This disturbance determines the behavior of nearly all other secondary effects seen in explosions.

arxiv-2307-13117.title: Towards α ′ \alpha^{\prime} -finiteness: q q -deformed open string amplitude
arxiv-2307-13117.creator: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun
arxiv-2307-13117.description: Abstract Revisiting the Coon amplitude, a deformation of the Veneziano amplitude with a logarithmic generalization of linear Regge trajectories, we scrutinize its potential origins in a worldsheet theory by proposing a definition of its q q -deformation through the integral representation of the q q -beta function.

arxiv-2406-02636.title: Strengthening Network Intrusion Detection in IoT Environments with Self-Supervised Learning and Few Shot Learning
arxiv-2406-02636.creator: Safa Ben Atitallah, Maha Driss, Wadii Boulila, Anis Koubaa
arxiv-2406-02636.description: Abstract The Internet of Things (IoT) has been introduced as a breakthrough technology that integrates intelligence into everyday objects, enabling high levels of connectivity between them. As the IoT networks grow and expand, they become more susceptible to cybersecurity attacks.

arxiv-2412-10683.title: Adaptive Nonparametric Perturbations of Parametric Models with Generalized Bayes
arxiv-2412-10683.creator: Bohan Wu bw2766@columbia.edu, Eli N. Weinstein enawe@dtu.dk, Sohrab Salehi sohrab.salehi@mskcc.org, Yixin Wang yixinw@umich.edu, David M. Blei david.blei@columbia.edu
arxiv-2412-10683.description: Abstract Parametric Bayesian modeling offers a powerful and flexible toolbox for machine learning. Yet the model, however detailed, may still be wrong, and this can make inferences untrustworthy. In this paper we introduce a new class of semiparametric corrections for parametric Bayesian models, when the target of inference is a functional of the true data distribution.

arxiv-2502-17020.title: Moving Past Single Metrics: Exploring Short-Text Clustering Across Multiple Resolutions
arxiv-2502-17020.creator: Justin K. Miller, Tristram J. Alexander
arxiv-2502-17020.description: Abstract Cluster number is typically a parameter selected at the outset in clustering problems, and while impactful, the choice can often be difficult to justify. Inspired by bioinformatics, this study examines how the nature of clusters varies with cluster number, presenting a method for determining cluster robustness, and providing a systematic method for deciding on the cluster number.

arxiv-2511-07894.title: From Natural Language to Certified H-infinity Controllers: Integrating LLM Agents with LMI-Based Synthesis
arxiv-2511-07894.creator: Shihao Li, Jiachen Li, Jiamin Xu, Dongmei Chen
arxiv-2511-07894.description: Abstract We present S2C (Specification-to-Certified-Controller), a multi-agent framework that maps natural-language requirements to certified ℋ ∞ \mathcal{H}_{\infty} state-feedback controllers via LMI synthesis. S2C coordinates five roles— SpecInt (spec extraction), Solv (bounded-real lemma (BRL) LMI), Tester (Monte Carlo and frequency-domain checks), Adapt (spec refinement), and CodeGen (deployable code).

pmc-11286875.creator: Allan J Kember, Hafsa Zia, Praniya Elangainesan, Min-En Hsieh, Ramak Adijeh, Ivan Li, Leah Ritchie, Sina Akbarian, Babak Taati, Sebastian R Hobson, Elham Dolatabadi
pmc-11286875.description: Sleeping on the back after 28 weeks of pregnancy has recently been associated with giving birth to a small-for-gestational-age infant and late stillbirth, but whether a causal relationship exists is currently unknown and difficult to study prospectively. This study was conducted to build a computer vision model that can automatically detect sleeping position in pregnancy under real-world conditions.

pmc-12950650.title: Clarifying the conflation of biochar carbon stability and its soil co-benefits
pmc-12950650.creator: Robert W. Brown, David R. Chadwick, Davey L. Jones
pmc-12950650.description: Not all biochar is equal. We clarify the frequent conflation between biochar carbon stability and soil co-benefits across research, policy, and markets. While stability ensures long-term carbon storage, co-benefits rely on more surface functionality from less stable biochar. Decoupling these dimensions enables designing biochar optimized for distinct functions.

pmc-13079961.title: Landscape of Aging Policies in Bangladesh: A Perspective Study
pmc-13079961.creator: Md Jamil Hossain
pmc-13079961.description: Background and AimsAging is currently a global concern, as there has been a massive transition in life expectancy and lower mortality rates because of advances in medical science. Bangladesh is experiencing a demographic transition with its elderly population, projected to reach 21% by 2050. This demographic shift raises significant social, economic, healthcare, and social inclusion challenges.

pmc-13353784.title: Non-absorbable antibiotics worsen alcohol-associated liver disease in gastric acid-suppressed mice
pmc-13353784.creator: Fernanda Raya Tonetti, Hui Han, Marcos F. Fondevila, Wenchao Wei, Burcin Özdirik, Jasmohan S. Bajaj, Mitchell L. Schubert, Masoumeh Sikaroodi, Patrick M. Gillevet, Sonja Lang, Münevver Demir, Imran R. Rahman, Wilfred A. van der Donk, Francisco Bosques-Padilla, Elizabeth C. Verna, Juan G. Abraldes, R
pmc-13353784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gastric acid-suppressive medications, particularly proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), are commonly used in patients with alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) to prevent and manage upper gastrointestinal bleeding, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory/aspirin-induced gastroesophageal damage. By inhibiting the gastric H⁺/K⁺-ATPase, PPIs suppress acid secretion and impair bacterial killing, thereby promoting gut dysbiosis that disrupts barrier integrity and enhances bacterial translocation, ultimately exacerbating liver injury.

pmc-13477260.title: Functional Sex Reversal in Adult Gonochoristic Teleosts is Mediated by Ovarian Germline Stem Cell Plasticity and Somatic Cell Transdifferentiation
pmc-13477260.creator: Yang Yang, Liechao Yu, Wanchang Zhang, Gary Wessel, Ruiyi Chen, Weihua Hu, Dongdong Xu
pmc-13477260.description: Sexual fate in vertebrates is generally considered developmentally fixed; however, teleost fishes exhibit remarkable flexibility in their reproductive systems. It remains unclear whether a fully differentiated gonochoristic vertebrate can undergo complete and functional sex reversal, or what molecular mechanisms could drive such reprogramming.

pmc-13628028.title: Impact of a Culturally Tailored Educational Intervention on Human Papillomavirus Knowledge and Vaccination Intentions Among Women in Saudi Arabia: Quasi-Experimental Study
pmc-13628028.creator: Ebtesam A Elsayed, Fathia Ahmed Mersal, Heba Ahmed Osman Mohamed, Ala M Aljehani, Najla M Aljehani
pmc-13628028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHuman papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide. Despite the availability of effective vaccines, uptake remains suboptimal in many settings, including Saudi Arabia, where cultural sensitivities, limited awareness, and vaccine hesitancy have been documented.
